en: The Scripture on the Ritual for the Recitation of the Heart Mantra of the Eleven-faced Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Volume One.
By the Kai-fu Yi-tong San-si, Te-jin, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Su.

The Imperial Preceptor, who held a fief of three thousand households, was invested with the purple robe and posthumously honored as Minister of Works; his posthumous title was Dajian (Great Mirror), and his formal name was the Tripitaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daguangzhi Daxingshan Temple. Translated by imperial decree: Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavān was dwelling in the palace of the Great Holy Avalokiteśvara on Mount Potalaka.
That mountain abounded with immeasurable śāla and tamāla trees.
It was adorned with various flowering trees, such as the campaka, the aśoka, the atimuktaka, and the tagara.
He was accompanied by a great assembly of eight thousand bhikṣus,
as well as ninety-nine koṭi-nayuta-hundred-thousand bodhisattvas,
and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of devas from the Śuddhāvāsa heavens.
With Īśvara, Maheśvara, and Brahmādevaputra as their leaders,
they surrounded him on all sides as he preached the Dharma.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara was surrounded by immeasurable vidyādhara sages.
Having approached the place where the World-Honored One was, and having arrived at the Buddha’s presence,
he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated the World-Honored One three times to the right,
withdrew to sit on one side, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Bhagavān, I have a heart-essence mantra called the Eleven Faces,
which has been proclaimed together by eleven koṭis of Tathāgatas;
I shall now speak it."
It brings benefit and happiness to all sentient beings,
can eliminate all diseases,
and quells all inauspiciousness and evil dreams.
Furthermore, it restrains untimely death,
causes those with impure faith to attain pure faith,
and is capable of removing all obstacles and vinayakas.
Because all that the mind hopes for is fulfilled accordingly,
I do not see anyone— in the world of devas, māras, or brahmās, nor among the assembly of śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas—
who can provide protection, rescue, or sustenance through such secret words of the mind as I do.
There shall be peace, auspiciousness, and exemption from punishment;
because one is freed from swords, staves, and poisons,
there is no possibility for anyone to transgress this.
Except for those whose past karma is not yet determined, all Tathāgatas praise and protect those who receive and uphold these secret words with a resolute mind.
All Tathāgatas rejoice in this. World-Honored One, I recall the past.
After the passage of as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges,
there will be a Tathāgata named Śatapuṣpanetra-śikhara-anāvaraṇa-vimala-balaprabhārāja.
At that time, I shall be a great ṛṣi.
Having received this secret mantra of the mind from that Tathāgata,
as soon as it was received, all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions appeared before him. Because he beheld all the Tathāgatas,
he immediately attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
This secret mantra possesses such a treasury of great merit.
If there are sons or daughters of good family who,
with pure faith and a heart of profound reverence, [engage with it...]
By attending with mindfulness,
one obtains ten kinds of benefits in this present life.
What are these ten?
First, one is free from all diseases;
second, one is embraced by all Tathāgatas;
third, one spontaneously obtains gold, silver, wealth, treasures, and various grains such as wheat.
Fourth, no enemies whatsoever shall be able to thwart or destroy them.
Fifth, kings and princes within the royal palace shall first address them with words of greeting and comfort.
Sixth, they shall not be harmed by poisons or malevolent sorcery.
Seventh, all diseases such as cold and heat shall not affect the body.
Eighth, one cannot be harmed by any blades or weapons,
nor can one be drowned by water.
Ninth, fire cannot burn them.
Tenth, they do not meet with untimely death.
Furthermore, they obtain four kinds of merit.
First, at the time of death, one shall behold the Tathāgata;
second, one shall not be reborn in the evil realms;
third, one shall not meet with an untimely death.
Fourth, from this world, one attains birth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
World-Honored One, I recall that in the past,
after ten *gaṅgā* sands of kalpas had passed...
There was a Buddha named Maṇḍāragandha Tathāgata.
At that time, I was a householder,
and from that Tathāgata I received this heart-mantra.
Having transcended and abandoned the cycle of birth and death for four hundred thousand kalpas,
by means of this secret mantra, through my day and night recitation and mental attention,
I have attained the Bodhisattva Liberation Dharma-gate of the Treasury of Wisdom of Great Compassion, in which all Buddhas abide.
All forms of bondage, impending execution,
water, fire, wind, thieves, malevolent poisons, curses, and sorcery,
as well as various hardships caused by humans and non-humans.
By this, I am able to act as a refuge, a protection, a consolation, an island, a dwelling,
and a superior destination for all sentient beings.
By the power of this mantra,
all violent yakṣas, rākṣasas, and others are first caused to give rise to a heart of compassion and pity;
thereafter, they are established and settled in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"Blessed One, this mantra of mine possesses such great majesty and power that by reciting it even once,
the four grave offenses are eliminated and one attains complete purification."
Even the five crimes of immediate retribution will be completely eliminated without remainder;
how much more so, then, will all other sins be extinguished?
That person shall obtain all the roots of goodness accumulated by immeasurable billions of nayutas of Buddhas.

If noble sons or noble daughters, bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas or upāsikās, brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, or others of any other kind, hear this secret mantra of the mind, whether they recite it or maintain it, all their wishes shall be fulfilled.
On the fourteenth or fifteenth day of the waxing moon,
fast for one day and one night for my sake,
maintaining purity and reciting the mantra.
One transcends forty thousand kalpas of birth and death.
For all sentient beings, the mere recitation of my name surpasses the recitation of the names of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Tathāgatas.
All shall attain non-retrogression,
be free from all illnesses,
and escape all untimely deaths and calamities.
One should distance oneself from unwholesome conduct of body, speech, and mind;
if one can act in accordance with the teachings,
one should apply the mind to contemplative practice.
The Buddha’s bodhi was as if held in the palm of his hand.
At that time, the Bhagavān praised the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, O Son of the Buddha!"
You have given rise to great compassion for all sentient beings;
by means of this skillful method,
you are able to establish all sentient beings in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"I rejoice deeply because you have received this prophecy;
you should now speak it.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara—
Rising from his seat, he adjusted his robes,
bared his right shoulder, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet,
and recited his own root mantra.
Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo ’ryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya tathāgatāya.
Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo sarvatathāgatavirājitasamyaksaṃbuddhānām. Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya.
Svāhā | Tathāgata-satvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya | Tadyathā | Rana rana rati rati | Svāhā.
Dhuru dhuru jñā vajre vajre prajñe kuṣme kuṣmavaśe ilimili cilicili cañcarāma paṇaya paramaḍḍha-sattva mahākāruṇika.
*Luṇika svāhā.* Next, the secret mantra for bathing, sprinkling, and purifying the robes is taught:

*Namo ratnatrayāya | namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | ha ha ha ha | iri miri cirī viri kile sire svāhā.* With this secret mantra, one consecrates the water.
For bathing, sprinkling, purifying the body, and cleansing the robes,
one should recite [the mantra] seven times.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva further spoke this secret mantra for offering incense:
*Tadyathā*: *cūru cūru ha ha ha ha svāhā*. With this secret mantra, empower incense by burning it as an offering.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara further spoke the secret mantra for offering flowers, saying:
*tadyathā | tsi li tsi li | dhi ri dhi ri | tsi ri tsi ri svāhā*. One should empower the flowers and lamps with this secret mantra and offer them while reciting it seven times.
Then, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara further spoke the secret mantra for the offering of food and drink, saying:
*Tadyathā sari sari siri siri suru suru svāhā*. One should empower the food, drink, and so forth with this secret mantra and offer it while reciting it twenty-one times.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this mantra for *homa*:
Tadyathā | hase mada se cale hulu hulu curu curu suru suru muru muru svāhā. With this mantra, one consecrates *jāti* wood and kindles the fire.
Dip both ends of a *jāti* wood stick with ghee, honey, and curdled milk,
and cast it into the fire to burn;
do not eat for a day and night.
Offer oblations into the fire twenty-one times,
and thereafter seek the accomplishment of the rite.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva further spoke the secret mantra for binding the boundaries of the directions:

*Tadyathā | iri miri cirimiri tirihiri svāhā*. With this secret mantra, one should empower water, white mustard seeds, or ashes for the purpose of establishing the boundary (*sīmābandha*); it should be recited seven times.
Then, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara further spoke this secret mantra for escorting the noble assembly back to their palace:
*Tadyathā | miṭi ṭuṭi ṭiṭi jeṣa jeṣa bhagavan nārīyavārucite śvāra svabhāvānāṃ svāhā*. Reciting this secret mantra, one should visualize escorting the Noble Ones back to their original palaces.
I shall now explain the benefits of recitation.
Even one who has not previously practiced it can accomplish all undertakings.
If there is a person suffering from a feverish illness, hot and cold chills, [they shall be cured].
If it manifests once every day, or once every two, three, or four days;
or if one is afflicted by spirits, mātṛkā-s, piśācas,
epilepsy, scrofula, or white leprosy.
As for cases involving *gū* poisons, venomous insects, and the like,
if one empowers earth and sesame seeds with white sandalwood incense seventeen times and applies them, the affliction will be cured immediately.
All karmic obstructions shall become completely purified.
If one suffers from malignant winds, by consecrating oil and applying it,
one will be healed immediately.
If one suffers from earache, [use] *śrīkhaṇḍa* (sandalwood) oil.
Boil the inner bark of the *huāpí* (birch) tree and drip [the decoction] into the ear;
the pain will immediately cease.
It can also cure hemicrania.
In all instances of illness,
as soon as this empowerment is recited, there is none that is not cured;
upon mere recitation, success is attained.
If one wishes to achieve accomplishment,
one should carve the body of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva from high-quality, flawless white sandalwood.
It is one chi and three cun in height;
it has eleven heads and four arms,
with the first hand on the right side holding a rosary.
The second right hand bestows fearlessness;
the first left hand holds a lotus flower,
and the second left hand grasps a kundaṭīka staff.
Of its eleven faces, the three faces in front display a peaceful aspect;
the three faces on the left display a wrathful aspect;
and the three faces on the right display the appearance of protruding sharp fangs.
The face on the back is made with a smiling and wrathful expression;
the uppermost face bears the marks of a Tathāgata.
Within each of the crowns upon their heads is a transformation Buddha.
Once the image of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, adorned with various kinds of necklaces and ornaments,
has been completed, it should be installed in a place where the relics of the Buddha are present.
The practitioner should then wear clean garments.
If a householder observes the eight precepts,
makes offerings at the three times of day, and performs an unlimited number of recitations,
they should place this image of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara in a pure location from the first day of the bright fortnight until the eighth day.
Facing west, consume milk or coarse wheat;
burn aloeswood, storax, and sandalwood incense according to one's means.
Continuing until the thirteenth day, one should consume the three white foods on that day and perform an extensive offering. Then,
one takes wood from a Bodhi tree and kindles a fire.
Furthermore, separately take pieces of bodhi tree wood,
ten finger-widths in length,
and anoint both ends with *śrīkhaṇḍa* (sahakāra) oil.
If one offers [the substance] into the homa fire-pit one thousand and eight times,
the earth will immediately tremble and the image will also move.
One will hear a voice emerging from the mouth at the very top of the image, praising the practitioner and saying:
Excellent, excellent, Son of the Buddha! Since you are able to seek and pray with such diligent perseverance,
I shall fulfill all your aspirations and grant you the accomplishment of soaring through the air and becoming invisible.
"O Vidyādhara Cakravartin Dharma King,
you shall surely attain such accomplishments as these, even to the point of being no different from me."
Furthermore, as for the second ritual procedure:
from the fifteenth day of the waxing moon,
one should install the image within the śarīra stūpa.
Without eating for day or night,
using one hundred and eight *jāti* flowers and *sumana* flowers, he recited the secret mantra once and cast each flower at the image as he struck it.
Then, directly in front of the image,
one shall let out a great roar;
the practitioner should not be afraid.
Then the earth will shake violently.
One should not interrupt the recitation and should immediately offer this prayer:
May I become a great refuge for all sentient beings who are without master and without support,
and may I fulfill every aspiration of all living beings.
They shall all be brought to fulfillment and attain freedom from obstacles.
Furthermore, regarding the mantra practitioner:
during a lunar eclipse, one should take one *liang* of clarified butter and place it in a silver vessel.
Recite the mantra seven times before the object;
whether one consumes it oneself or gives it to another,
all illnesses shall be cured.
How much more so if one fails to attain *siddhi* through recitation from the first waning of the moon until it becomes full again? Furthermore,
regarding the practitioner of secret mantras (*mantrin*):
First, having bathed and purified oneself, and wearing clean garments,
take realgar or cow bezoar and recite the heart-mantra one thousand and eight times before the image.
Three signs will appear;
thereafter, by marking the forehead, one shall attain three kinds of accomplishments according to their efficacy— superior, middling, or inferior.
If one uses this mixed with water to bathe the body,
all obstacles and difficulties will be eliminated,
and one will remain far removed from all evil dreams and inauspicious omens.
One shall obtain all forms of auspiciousness and prosperity;
all pestilences shall be completely cured and healed.
Furthermore, one should offer incense and flowers to the noble Avalokiteśvara.
Take some collyrium and empower it one hundred and eight times.
Apply it to the slightly wrathful face on the left side of the forehead;
this will subjugate all enemy armies.
Furthermore, if there is an epidemic among humans, cattle, or other livestock,
one should face Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and take *kaṭphala* wood,
dip it in mustard oil, and [proceed as follows].
One should perform the homa ritual.
Using crimson thread, one should twist it into a cord to the right,
with a thickness like that of a copper chopstick.
Make two strands;
recite [the mantra] once for each knot, up to seven knots.
Tie them beneath the neck or in the hair-knot of the patient.
Then the epidemic will be eliminated, stilled, and one will be liberated.
Furthermore, for one who is possessed by various malevolent spirits such as the Ḍākinīs,
take white thread and empower it as before.
Tie it to a peaceful face and let it remain overnight.
Then, take twenty-one knots,
reciting the secret mantra once for each knot as you tie them.
If one ties [this] around the neck of a sick person, they will immediately be cured.
Furthermore, if there are enemies or calamities such as epidemics that threaten to enter the borders of a kingdom,
and one wishes to bind the boundaries of the cardinal directions, [one should perform this rite].
Burn incense of *kunkuma* and perform *homa*.
Take a five-colored thread, empower it with mantras,
and tie it to the face of the one who is tranquil.
Thus, one establishes a firm and greatly majestic boundary for the cardinal and intermediate directions.
Furthermore, if a practitioner of secret mantras wishes to engage in debate with an adversary and desires to achieve victory:
One should make offerings to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Burn *vāsaka* wood and *kalāya* seeds,
and empower a white thread one hundred and eight times.
If it is bound to the wrathful face,
all disputes, quarrels, and legal litigations will be entirely overcome and brought to cessation.
If it is bound to the peaceful face, [the same result follows].
This can remove all obstacles and difficulties.
Furthermore, one may bathe the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with various fragrances mixed with water.
Furthermore, by consecrating the image of Vināyaka with one hundred and eight recitations of the *Āśvāsana-svayambhū* mantra while bathing it,
all obstacles and difficulties will be entirely extinguished.

The Scripture on the Ritual Manual for the Heart Recitation of the Eleven-Faced Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
Middle Volume.
By Kai-fu Yi-san-si Te-jin Shi Hong-lu-qing, Duke of Su State.

The Imperial Preceptor, who held a fief of three thousand households, was invested with the purple robe and posthumously honored as Minister of Works; his title was Dajian (Great Mirror), and he was the Tripitaka Master Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery. This ritual manual was translated by imperial decree. It is applicable for the recitation and invocation of all deities belonging to the Lotus Family.
I shall now explain the ritual procedures for practice,
which apply universally to all methods of Avalokiteśvara,
including the rites of binding protection, invitation, and offering.
The practitioner should first bathe to purify the body and don clean garments;
then, in a pure place before a sacred image,
they should form the samaya-mudrā of their respective family.
Join the two hands in the lotus-palms gesture (*padmakośa-mudrā*),
with the remaining six fingers extended like an opening lotus flower.
The *samaya-mantra* of the family of Avalokiteśvara is as follows:
Oṃ paṇamovāya svāhā. Next, one should empower water for bathing, whether at a river, a pond, or in a bathhouse.
The mantra for consecrating the water is as follows:
*Namo ratnatrayāya | namo ’ryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya | oṃ samaye svāmine śānte dānte sarvasamayānupraviṣṭānurāge svāhā*. Then, enter the pool.
Alternatively, for taking water for bathing, one forms the *śvāsavaha-mudrā* to accomplish the Lotus Family (*padmakula*) activities: with both hands, the right presses down upon the left;
the fingers are interlaced within to form fists.
Join the middle fingers and slightly bend their first joints;
bend the two index fingers and place them upon the upper joints of the middle fingers without touching them, forming the shape of a vajra. The mantra is as follows:
Namo mahāśriye oṃ śodhaye samaye svāmine siddhi siddhi sādhaya śive ti śaṅkari śvaṃmine āvāhaya sarvārthasādhani svāhā. With this mudrā, protect the body.
Expel the vināyakas, as well as [obstacles regarding] incense, flowers, food, drink, and so forth;
remove all impurities and cause [the site] to shine with brilliance.
Next, bind the Amṛtakuṇḍalī mudrā.
It should be employed with mental visualization during the time of bathing, in conjunction with the secret mantra.
Interlace the two little fingers with their palms facing each other,
double-bend the two ring fingers,
and press them against the space between the interlaced fingers.
Join the middle fingers vertically.
Bend the two index fingers so they touch the back of the upper joints of the middle fingers,
not quite touching, like a vajra.
Place the thumbs side by side and extend them upward, aligned with the sides of the middle fingers.
Recite the mantra:

*Namo ratnatrayāya | namaḥ śrīvajrapāṇaye mahāyakṣasenāpataye | namo vajrakrodhāya | oṃ hulu hulu tiṣṭha tiṣṭha bandha bandha hana hana amṛte hūṃ phaṭ*. Next, perform the mudrā for empowering the earth: clench the four fingers of the right hand into a fist, grasping the thumb.
Press the mudrā upon the earth;
divide that earth into three portions for ablution,
and empower them with this secret mantra.
The mantra is:
Oṃ pūrṇa-jvala hūṃ. [Recite this] at all places touched by impurity;
it protects one's own body.
To employ the wrathful Ucchuṣma mudrā for touching the body:
form a fist with the right hand and extend the thumb,
applying it to five locations.
That is to say, recite [the mantra] once each at the forehead, the right shoulder, the left shoulder, the heart, and the throat.
At the crown of the head, disperse the secret mantra, saying:
*Oṃ krodhana hūṃ jaḥ*. Having finished washing the hands and rinsing the mouth:
One should perform the *śucimudrā*:
turn the right palm upward and bend the ring finger into the palm.
Place the root of the thumb and the index finger together.
Using this mudrā, receive the water and drink it three times;
wipe the lips twice.
Next, seal the two eyes, the two nostrils, the two ears, the two shoulders, the heart, and the navel;
sprinkle water on the two feet.
Again, take water and sprinkle it over the body.
The mantra is:
Oṃ kī kīle kuru svāhā. Then, at the side of a bathhouse or a river or pond, divide the earth and so forth into three heaps.
Use one portion to wash from the feet to the waist;
the second portion from the waist to the neck;
and the third portion from the neck to the head.
When the bathing is completed,
one should then direct the mind toward the Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, and the tutelary deity Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
and scoop up water with the mudrā.
Directing the mind toward bathing the assembly of noble ones,
one should look upward with both palms joined;
the backs of the six fingers from the middle finger downward are pressed together, while the two tips of the nails of the index fingers are made visible.
To form this seal, one should interlace the sides of the two thumbs. This seal is common to all [practices]. The secret mantra for the bathing of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva is:
*Namo ratnatrayāya, namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya, tadyathā, jvale mahājvale sarvabuddhi svāhā*. Next, bind the *argha* seal.
Gazing upward, join the palms with the two thumbs each pressing against the tips of the index fingers.
Scooping up water to offer as *argha*, recite the secret mantra:
*Oṃ devī buddhasvāhā*. Thereafter, using the mudrā, scoop up water and sprinkle it over yourself for consecration.
Visualize the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara holding the vase of nectar;
his body emits radiance as he is surrounded by a multitude of holy beings,
while the devas play exquisite music.
Visualize that Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva pours nectar into the body of the mantra-practitioner.
For the Muṇḍarī mudrā:
place both index fingers upon the upper joints of the middle fingers.
Placing the two thumbs behind [the hands] and resting them against the sides of the index fingers,
the secret mantra is: *Namo mahāśrīye oṃ hara hara mahāvijaye dhuna dhuna bhañja bhañjaya duṣṭakṛtān dūra dūra vidhvaṃsaya svara*.

*Gicce minni binne binde hana hana vijina vina ya jñāpaya jñāpaya sarvakalikaluṣa-pratibhāna-śrīye ṭve ṭve mañje mañje vajre vajre jvālani śokye jvālani śodhaya svāhā.* When the ritual bath (*snāna*) is completed, [recite this].
Then, take a pure cloth and empower it with this mantra of the Tathāgata’s robe.
All garments one wears shall become the Tathāgata’s robe. The mantra is as follows: [Mantra]
Oṃ rakṣa rakṣa sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhitam ātmānaṃ jīvāraya svāhā. Recite this seven times.
Having put on his robes,
he emerged from the bathing area and proceeded toward the clean chamber.
Free from greed, hatred, and delusion,
one should not look upon foul, impure, or miscellaneous objects, nor at outcastes (*caṇḍāla*) and other base persons.
One should instead contemplate a full moon disc within the center of one's own chest.
This very moon disc is formed of natural luminosity;
the bodhicitta is perfectly pure and white like a stainless moon disc.
Furthermore, visualize the syllable *hṛīḥ* upon the face of the moon disc.
Like the color of red crystal,
it emits light that illuminates the worlds of the ten directions;
within that radiance, one's own body becomes the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
They are equal and without distinction.
With the left hand in the vajra-fist, he holds a lotus at his left hip;
with the right hand, it is placed against his own heart.
Like the unfolding of a lotus flower,
one contemplates that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure,
unstained by the dust and grime of the afflictions.
He resembles a lotus flower;
his body is surrounded by a circular halo,
and upon his crown is the Tathāgata Amitāyus.
Adorned with various precious necklaces and garlands,
he stepped upon an eight-petaled lotus flower and arrived outside the door of the meditation chamber.
Sprinkle [water] as before,
and then one should perform the empowerment upon the crown of the head by forming a fist with the right hand.
Pressing the thumb and index finger together, one should place the seal upon the crown of the head and recite the heart-mantra of Tārā Bodhisattva:
Oṃ kuru kule svāhā. Then, enter the vihāra.
Mentally recollect all the worthy ones and sages;
with earnest devotion, prostrate yourself with the five limbs touching the ground, and with your right knee on the earth,
gaze upon all the Tathāgatas and great Bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions.
Visualizing all worthy ones and sages as if they were before one's eyes,
one confesses and reveals transgressions, rejoices in merit, requests [the Buddhas] to teach, makes vows, and dedicates the merit toward unsurpassed bodhi;
then, one sits in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*).

One should immediately form the samaya mudrā of one's own family; this also applies generally to the recitation of all Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattvas. First, one should employ Tārā Bodhisattva for the protection of the body;
Bhṛkuṭī Bodhisattva is likewise especially excellent.
Alternatively, it is also applicable for those who recite other Great Kings of the Four Vidyās of Great Majestic Power.
As for the mudrā of the Noble Tārā Bodhisattva:
interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward to form fists.
Join the index fingers upright, like unopened blue lotus flowers. The mantra is: *Namo* (as above). The mantra for consecrating the water is:
*Oṃ tāre tuttāre ture svāhā*. Next, the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Bhṛkuṭī is explained.
As with the Tārā mudrā above, slightly bend the blue lotus.
The mantra is: Homage as above.
Oṃ sara sara jaye svāhā. Next, the mudrās of the four vidyārājas are explained.
First, interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward.
Place the mudrā upon the crown of the head. The secret mantra is as follows:
Oṃ bāva āsepara. [With] the two palms covering one's own mouth, the secret mantra of the mouth-mudrā is:
Āḥ. Next, form the lotus mudrā.
As above, form the mudrā of the blossoming lotus and place it at the navel.
The mantra of this mudrā is as follows:
Oṃ bānām bānām mahābānāṃ padmadharanīlaraktapāṇigatāya svāhā. Next, form the mudrā of Hayagrīva Vidyārāja.
First, perform the vajra-joined palms;
join the two middle fingers upright,
and with the two index fingers, each hook the tips of the ring fingers.
Each index finger presses upon the upper joint of its respective middle finger;
the two little fingers are held upright, inserted into the palms,
and joined together with the two thumbs, which are also held upright.
The mantra is:
Oṃ amṛtodbhava udbhava hūṃ phaṭ. Having performed the ritual expulsion with this seal and mantra, [proceed].
Next, bind the boundary of the earth and the boundary of the maṇḍala.
Hook the two thumbs together,
then spread them apart and extend all the fingers upright.
Raising the palms like the wings of a hawk,
one binds the boundaries of the cardinal and intermediate directions.
The secret mantra is as follows:
Namo ratnatrayāya | Namo jinarṣabhāya vighnahararājāya tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya ||
Namo sarvatathāgatebhyo vīra-ha-vīryebhyaḥ samyak-saṃbuddhebhyaḥ | Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya ||
*Mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā | iri miri kiri miri viri hiri svāhā.* With this mantra,
empower the scented water.
Recite this once to bind the boundaries of the cardinal directions and intermediate points;
next, bind the boundary of the maṇḍala by interlacing the fingers of both hands with the palms facing inward.
Open the palms and join the index fingers upright;
bring the two thumbs together, extending them downward as much as possible.
The mantra is:
Āḥ lu li: one should employ this mudrā and mantra for the purpose of binding the maṇḍala boundary.
Furthermore, the mantra for the rite of expulsion is:
Oṃ iri iri iraṇa gaviḷa vaya ve niṃ svāhā. Next, the mantra for purifying the space-element is taught:
Oṃ paṇamite svāhā. With this secret mantra, empower the incense burner.
Rotate it upward and recite seven times.
First, prepare an argha vessel made of conch shell, gold, or silver.
Refined copper, pure leaves,
tiles, and wooden vessels—
such items as these are praised.
Fill the argha vessel with scented water and flowers;
according to the four types of objectives to be sought,
place flowers of the four colors before the mandala.
One should visualize the maṇḍala as a great ocean of milk.
Recite this secret mantra:
Oṃ vimalodake hūṃ. With both hands, interlace the fingers with the palms facing upward and rotate them.
It immediately becomes a great ocean of nectar.
Within that ocean, one contemplates Mount Sumeru,
which is composed of the four precious substances.
Adorned with the intermingled splendor of immeasurable various jewels,
one forms fists by crossing the two hands palm-to-palm inward and recites this secret mantra:
Recite the mantra "Oṃ ajara hūṃ" while forming this mudrā.
Contemplate that a mountain of jewels has emerged from the great ocean,
and then visualize a jeweled pavilion upon that mountain.
That palace was composed of immeasurable varieties of precious jewels;
everywhere, strings of pearls and necklaces were suspended,
and bells and silken banners were stirred by a gentle breeze.
It emitted harmonious and elegant sounds,
adorned with various interspersed mani-jewels, half-moons, full moons, and the like;
furthermore, immeasurable articles of offering filled the pavilion.
Within that palace, one contemplates the Great Maṇḍala.
While performing this visualization, one interlaces the ten fingers with the right hand placed over the left, beginning from the tips.
Then, one recites the mantra for the Universal Offering.
He immediately sent a carriage adorned with the seven precious gems to deliver [the seal] to the place of the Noble One.
As for that seal, the two hands are placed with the palms facing inward and the fingers interlaced.
